_fixture: NOT OWNED HARDWARE. Exercises the dc-gearmotor type, and finds a gap while doing it.
This one is PARTIAL. The stall figure and the no-load speed fit the existing
voltage-indexed rows exactly. What has no home is Pololu's third published figure:
a GEARBOX torque limit of 4 kg-cm, which at this ratio is BELOW the 4.7 kg-cm the
motor can stall at - so it is the binding constraint on the whole actuator and the
schema cannot record it. See the note, and Knowledge/concepts/open-questions.md.

source.citation: Pololu product page for the 34:1 25D MP 12V gearmotor: 4.7 kg-cm stall torque, 1.8 A stall current at 12 V. Converted at 1 kgf-cm = 0.0980665 N-m exactly, so 4.7 x 0.0980665 = 0.46091255. The source figure carries two significant figures.

Same page: 230 RPM no-load speed and 80 mA free-run current at 12 V. 230 rev/min x 2pi / 60 = 24.08554367752175 rad/s. Unlike the MG90S, this figure IS labelled no-load by the vendor, so it belongs in this field.

torque_limit.how_determined: Pololu, 25D family: 'the recommended upper limit for continuously applied loads is 4 kg-cm (55 oz-in)' and 'the recommended upper limit for intermittently permissible torque is 8 kg-cm (110 oz-in)'. Published in kg-cm and converted at 1 kgf-cm = 0.0980665 N-m exactly. Recorded as a GEARBOX property because the figures are identical at every ratio and every power tier in the family, which a motor thermal rating would not be.

source.citation: Pololu 25D Metal Gearmotors category page, applying to the whole family.
Published as '34:1'. Recorded as the nominal published ratio; Pololu documents exact ratios for some gearboxes in its datasheet, which was not read here.
Pololu 12V Medium-Power 25D specifications: stall current 1.8 A, typical free-run current 100 mA for the family; this variant's page gives 80 mA.

Pololu 34:1 Metal Gearmotor 25Dx52L mm MP 12V, product page specifications, read 2026-08-23 while sweeping the actuator type enum for coverage. Figures come from the product page; Pololu's 5 MB family datasheet with per-version performance graphs was not read.

note:
THE GAP THIS FIXTURE EXPOSED, NOW CLOSED BY ADR-0027. The 4 kg-cm figure lives in gearbox.torque_limit and no longer sits in this note for want of a field.

WHY IT IS A CEILING AND NOT A CAPACITY, which is the whole of ADR-0027. Pololu says 'do not exceed'; continuous_torque_nm means 'can sustain'. Different claims. The proof is at the other end of the family: the 9.7:1 HP variant stalls at 3.9 kg-cm while the ceiling is 4 kg-cm, so treating the ceiling as a capacity would promise a torque that motor cannot produce at all.

AND THAT THE FIGURE DOES NOT MOVE is what proves it belongs to the geartrain. It is identical at every ratio and every power tier in the 25D family - a motor thermal rating would vary with both.

continuous_torque_nm is STILL null, and capacity is still underivable, because Pololu publishes no thermal rating for the motor. The real continuous torque is min(gearbox ceiling, unpublished thermal limit) and only one of those is known. What the ceiling buys is a REFUSAL: a required torque above 0.392266 N-m is a sound no, which is the same asymmetry ADR-0015 rests on.

STILL NOT CONSUMED BY A DERIVATION. hold raises incomplete on the missing continuous rating before any load is computed, so wiring the ceiling in means restructuring that path - and no robot in data/ uses a geared actuator with a limit, so the change would ship untested against real data. The cross-check in validate.py reads the field today; hold reading it is the obvious next step.
